title: Everywhere now
hook: Buddhist communities in Europe, Africa, Latin America and beyond
carry: a good man pervades every place

segments.voice: Yesterday: vipassana went west, rising, falling, hearing, thinking. Your line: insight travels.

Three postcards. From Brazil: a temple in São Paulo, incense, a family bowing before a Japanese altar, and a conversation in Portuguese afterward over tea. From South Africa: a large temple with curved roofs on the grass near Pretoria, built by a Buddhist order from Taiwan. From Germany: a quiet house on a hill on the northern edge of Berlin, with steps up to a shrine room, where monks from Sri Lanka live. Three continents, one teaching.
screen: `A TEMPLE IN SÃO PAULO.` → `A TEMPLE NEAR PRETORIA.` → `A HOUSE IN BERLIN.`

segments.voice: When people move, their practice moves with them. Japanese families in Brazil built temples, just as they did in Hawaii and California. Sri Lankan, Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese, Korean and Tibetan communities have done the same in cities across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Australia, sometimes starting in a living room before there was a building. Others came to the teaching through books and travel. In Berlin, a doctor named Paul Dahlke built a house for Buddhist practice, and it still stands as a temple. And some Asian orders built temples abroad on purpose. The Taiwanese order Fo Guang Shan built Nan Hua Temple in South Africa, near Pretoria, and from it monks and nuns have taught in other parts of Africa. Look at the road since the poem. The Light of Asia put the Buddha's life into English verse. In Chicago, the teaching spoke for itself. Zen came west in a cup of tea. Temples kept their practice going behind a fence. Tibetan teachers carried a tradition over the mountains. Insight came west as noting. And now, everywhere. The Dhammapada, in Max Müller's words, compares the good to a scent that goes where flowers can't, and ends the verse: "a good man pervades every place." A teaching that began on foot in northern India now has shrine rooms on continents far from where it began.
screen: `FAMILIES BRING THEIR TEMPLES.` · `SEEKERS BUILD CENTERS.` · `ORDERS SEND TEACHERS.` · `A WEEK OF CROSSINGS.` · then, large: `EVERYWHERE NOW.`

segments.voice: Choose a place far from where you're sitting, and picture a small shrine room there, a few people sitting, maybe at this very hour, in a language you don't speak. Breathe in, and know they're breathing too. Breathe out, and sit with them across the distance.
Everywhere now. Temples in São Paulo, near Pretoria and in Berlin, built by families, seekers and orders, far from where the teaching began.
Your line: a good man pervades every place. Like a scent, it goes where flowers can't. Another week, done.
